A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PARTICULATE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary material. Their shared content and revisions can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and articulation experiments, ablations, generated-mesh demonstrations, and supplementary category-level results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and reports revised benchmark results, an additional feature ablation, and prediction variability.

M1.justification: The prediction heads, losses, matching, and mesh reconstruction procedures are retained. However, v1 Section 3.2 explicitly includes cross-attention in both directions, whereas v2 lists only query self-attention and query-to-point cross-attention. The PDFs do not establish whether this omission is editorial or an architecture change.

E1.justification: Lightwheel evaluation expands from 13 to 14 categories, adding sinks, with category-level results in v2 Table 8. The training datasets, PartNet-Mobility evaluation, and generated-mesh scenarios remain.

E2.justification: The segmentation comparisons retain PartField, P3SAM, SINGAPO, Articulate AnyMesh, and the Naive Baseline. Motion comparisons retain SINGAPO, Articulate AnyMesh, and the Naive Baseline, including the same connectivity and best-of-10 variants.

E3.justification: The stated Lightwheel evaluation size changes from 220 to 243 objects. Table 4 now describes evaluation on a subset of Lightwheel, while retaining the original A–C scores; this does not establish that those ablations were rerun. Training budgets, preprocessing, metrics, and baseline evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 4 add a control removing pre-trained PartField features. Its rest-state mIoU is 0.491 versus 0.551 for the full model on the ablation subset. Existing training-data and axis-parameterization ablations, metric analyses, and failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Tables 5–6 newly report PARTICULATE standard deviations across 10 predictions for both datasets, connectivity variants, and penalized/unpenalized metrics. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting beyond v1's point estimates. It does not establish repeated training runs or an increase in runs; SINGAPO's existing best-of-10 reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Central and supplementary results are extensively revised. With connectivity, Lightwheel rest-state gIoU changes from 0.286 to 0.332 and articulated-state gIoU from 0.259 to 0.305, alongside benchmark expansion, so these are not same-setting gains. PartNet-Mobility rest-state gIoU changes from 0.901 to 0.880. Sink results and the feature-removal ablation are added.

T1.justification: Section 3.5 corrects the definition of the predicted part count: v1 counts distinct point-level labels, whereas v2 defines P as the size of Q_A, the labels surviving face-level majority assignment. These counts need not coincide. The remaining mathematical formulation is retained, with equations reordered or made inline.

C1.justification: Both versions claim fast, feed-forward recovery of complete articulations, generalization to generated meshes, and a challenging benchmark with improved evaluation metrics. The rewritten abstract and introduction preserve these contributions; the conclusion is substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: The axis-regression footnote replaces the explicit mode-collapse explanation with a more qualified account of axis-location learning difficulty. Tables 7–8 explicitly identify five categories absent from training. The principal limitations concerning unfamiliar kinematics, missing interiors, and inter-part penetration remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies random tie-breaking for face assignments and a coordinate-wise median for axis voting. New Table 7 supplies category counts and training-distribution membership. These are additional implementation and dataset disclosures, without evidence of changed training hardware, hyperparameters, or resource access.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a bounded comparison with automatic rigging, citing Anymate, RigAnything, MagicArticulate, Farm3D, MagicPony, and Learning the 3D Fauna of the Web. ImageNet and the Cameras as Rays analogy citation are removed. The main positioning against articulation-generation and segmentation methods remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and substantial portions of the method undergo extensive rewriting and compression. Terminology shifts toward point/part tokens, the axis explanation is reorganized, and ablation paragraphs are reordered. These edits substantially revise exposition despite retaining the section hierarchy.

P2.justification: All five figures retain their illustrations, with Figures 4–5 relocated. Table 4 gains a feature column and ablation row; Tables 5–6 are resized to display uncertainty. A category-count table is added, and the former Table 7 becomes Table 8 with a sink column and green out-of-distribution highlighting.

improvement.justification: The new PartField ablation, prediction-level standard deviations, and explicit benchmark composition improve empirical support and transparency. These gains are limited by the unspecified ablation subset and the loss of precision in the attention-block description. Overall quality improves modestly; the changed Lightwheel scores alone do not demonstrate better performance under comparable conditions.
